text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: high error-rate detected for service="inference-runtime" region=us-west-2. Trigger: 5xx-rate > 0.5% for 5m. Root thread ts=1789501234

morgan: saw the alert. I'm on it — switching to oncall context. any immediate mitigation? :running_shirt_with_sash:

alex: repro'd. Model workers kept OOMing when seq_len spiked on a small subset of requests. Rolling restart of the worker pool reduced errors but we saw a degradation window.

elena: current status: new deploy rollback + instance recycle in progress. Traffic routing to fallback-model-2 enabled at 02:22 UTC. :thumbsup:

sam: flagging potential customer impact — a handful of high-traffic tenants may have seen increased errors and latency between 02:15 and 02:28 UTC. Need an estimate for affected requests and minutes of degraded service to assess SLA eligibility.

alex: quick check commands (obs query) i ran, paste if useful:
```
# observability ad-hoc (example)
SELECT count(*)
FROM requests
WHERE service = 'inference-runtime'
  AND status >= 500
  AND region = 'us-west-2'
  AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-15T02:15:00Z' AND '2026-03-15T02:28:00Z'
GROUP BY bin(1m, ts)
```

morgan: results: peak ~1.8k 5xx/min, total ~15k 5xx in that 13m window. P95 latency jumped from 200ms -> 3.4s. Fallback routing kept overall system up but lots of customer errors returned 503.

priya: thanks — I'll start the SLA eligibility checklist. We need: 1) customer-visible downtime window, 2) percentage of requests failed for tenant(s), 3) owning plan (SLA terms), 4) support rep + billing case. Can someone paste tenant IDs impacted?

elena: exporting list now, pushing to shared drive. short list: acct_8472, acct_9120, acct_3301. acct_8472 saw ~98% success (brief spikes), acct_9120 saw 18% failures, acct_3301 saw 9% failures.

sam: account rep for acct_9120 is @sam (that's me) — I'm prepping an account message but need the official tally and a suggested credit number.

morgan: to compute a conservative credit: follow SLA doc: hosted SLA = 99.9% monthly availability -> if availability < 99.9% then pro-rated credit tiers apply. Rough downtime for acct_9120: ~13 minutes of elevated errors + some request failures after failover; I'll calculate effective unavailable minutes as 18% failure ratio over the 13m window -> ~2.3 equivalent unavailable minutes, but operationally we'd treat the whole 13m window as degraded for customer notice.

alex: agree with conservative window approach. For billing, usually we count the full impacted window. Priya, billing wants an explicit formula we can paste:
```
# pro forma credit calc (to fill in)
impacted_window_minutes = 13
monthly_minutes = 30 * 24 * 60  # approx 43200
availability = 1 - (impacted_window_minutes / monthly_minutes)
# compare to SLA threshold (0.999) and compute credit tier per SLA doc
```

priya: grabbing SLA tiers now. If availability < 99.9% but >= 99.0% -> 10% credit; <99.0% and >=95.0% -> 25% credit; <95.0% -> 50% credit (example tiers). With a 13m window we're nowhere near big tiers, likely 10% if we count whole-month impact. I'll open billing case and attach the raw logs.

billing-bot: new billing case created: CASE-2026-5412 by priya. Please attach: incident id, affected accounts, start/end times, observability export CSV.

sam: drafting customer message — want to match tone to our other incident comms. Suggest short explanation, what we did, how we're preventing recurrence, and the credit statement (if eligible). Putting draft below:

"sam: Hi <Customer>, we experienced a service degradation impacting inference requests in us-west-2 between 2026-03-15T02:15Z and 2026-03-15T02:28Z. During this window some requests returned 503 errors. We rolled back a deploy and routed traffic to a fallback model to restore service. We're continuing an RCA to prevent recurrence. Based on our SLA, this incident meets the criteria for a pro-rated service credit; our billing team will follow up with the exact credit amount and next steps. We apologize for the disruption and are happy to coordinate any follow-up"

morgan: looks good. small tweak: remove 'meets the criteria' until priya confirms. change to: "we are evaluating eligibility for a pro-rated service credit"

sam: updated.

elena: ops note for internal RCA: root cause appears to be a combination of a model change that increased memory usage for certain long inputs + insufficient guardrails for seq_len. mitigation items: 1) revert model variant in staged clusters, 2) add seq_len validation and reject with 4xx for overly long requests, 3) improve autoscaling pre-warm heuristics.

alex: will own the code changes and can have a PR up within the day for seq_len validation. Will also add a canary with tighter memory limits.

priya: next steps from billing side: 1) compute affected-minute window per account (we have the CSV), 2) compute credit % per SLA and quantify $ amount, 3) confirm with finance and attach to CASE-2026-5412, 4) coordinate customer email once amount is confirmed. I will ping finance (cc @finance) separately.

morgan: oncall handoff: I'll do a short handover summary for the next shift. Note the rollback and fallback routing are stable; no ongoing alerts after 02:40Z. If anything new pops up escalate to eng-sre.

sam: once priya has the number I'll prepare the customer-specific draft including the dollar credit and next steps. Priya, can you aim to have a provisional credit calc in the case within 2 hours?

priya: yes — aiming for 2 hours. I'll attach the observability CSV and the sample calc.

alex: tagging the PR to the incident: link to PR when ready. Also will add a short automated test to catch memory regressions on long inputs.

incident-bot: incident status updated -> mitigation: traffic routed to fallback-model-2, deploy rollback initiated, errors decreasing. Incident state: monitoring.

morgan: thanks everyone. quick reactions: :thumbsup: :raised_hands: — feel free to close this thread when billing case has next steps and account email is queued.

priya: CASE-2026-5412 updated with attachments and pro-forma calc. moving to finance review.

billing-bot: note: once finance signs off we will issue a credit memo; make sure account team chooses whether to apply the credit automatically or wait for customer acceptance.

sam: got it. I'll follow up with acct_9120 and let them know we're evaluating a credit and will send details.

morgan: closing notes for handoff: RCA-in-progress, mitigation complete, oncall handing to night shift with brief. If anything else, ping me.

elena: leaving final log link here: https://internal.redwood/incident/1789501234/logs (internal)

morgan: thread resolved for now.

"""
